stage2: test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo 'working tree is not clean: the artifact would not be the revision under test'; exit 1; }
cargo build --release -p llama-helper && mkdir -p frontend/src-tauri/binaries && cp target/release/llama-helper frontend/src-tauri/binaries/llama-helper-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
cd frontend && npx --yes pnpm@11 run build && ./node_modules/.bin/tauri build --bundles appimage --config '{"build":{"beforeBuildCommand":""},"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'

umask 077; S2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/backchannel-stage2.XXXXXX) && mkdir -p "$S2/home" && printf '%s\n' "$S2" > .git/backchannel-stage2-root && git rev-parse HEAD > "$S2/expected-sha" && APP=$(ls -t target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage | head -1) && test -x "$APP" && printf '%s\n' "$APP" > "$S2/app"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && APP=$(cat "$S2/app") && (HOME="$S2/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$S2/home/.config" XDG_DATA_HOME="$S2/home/.local/share" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$S2/home/.cache" nohup "$APP" > "$S2/stdout.log" 2>&1 & echo $! > "$S2/pid") && sleep 20 && kill -0 "$(cat "$S2/pid")"
S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && orca-ide status --json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['ok'] and d['result']['runtime']['state']=='ready', d"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && PID=$(cat "$S2/pid") && orca-ide computer list-apps --json | PID="$PID" python3 -c "import json,sys,os; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert any(a['pid']==int(os.environ['PID']) for a in d['result']['apps']), 'app not visible to computer-use'"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && PID=$(cat "$S2/pid") && T=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('frontend/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json'))['app']['windows'][0]['title'])") && orca-ide computer list-windows --app pid:$PID --json | T="$T" python3 -c "import json,sys,os; d=json.load(sys.stdin); w=d['result']['windows']; assert len(w)==1 and w[0]['title']==os.environ['T'] and not w[0]['isMinimized'], w"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && PID=$(cat "$S2/pid") && orca-ide computer get-app-state --app pid:$PID --no-screenshot --json > "$S2/state.json" && python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); t=d['result']['snapshot']['treeText']; assert 'heading Welcome to' in t, t[:800]; assert 'push button Get Started' in t, t[:800]; print('first-launch screen present:', d['result']['snapshot']['elementCount'], 'elements')" "$S2/state.json"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && kill "$(cat "$S2/pid")"; sleep 2; S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && case "$S2" in /tmp/backchannel-stage2.*) ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac && test -d "$S2" && rm -rf -- "$S2" && rm -f -- .git/backchannel-stage2-root
scripts/audio-harness.sh up || { echo 'audio harness could not come up: the audio half of this gate cannot run, and a verdict must say so rather than skip it'; exit 1; }

umask 077; A2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/backchannel-stage2-audio.XXXXXX) && APP=$(ls -t target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage | head -1) && scripts/stage2-record-check.sh "$APP" "$A2" 'ask not' 'country'; RC=$?; APID=$(cat "$A2/pid" 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$APID" ] && { kill -TERM -"$APID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$APID" 2>/dev/null; }; sleep 4; [ -n "$APID" ] && kill -KILL -"$APID" 2>/dev/null; case "$A2" in /tmp/backchannel-stage2-audio.*) rm -rf -- "$A2" ;; esac; scripts/audio-harness.sh down; exit $RC
verification.notes: Product: a Tauri 2 desktop app (Linux AppImage/.deb, macOS .dmg, Windows .exe); artifact_kind 'cli' is the closest kind in the schema for a locally installed application. Development and every verification run happen on Linux only (ADR 0005); macOS and Windows are built in CI and are never proven here - a verdict names them as not proven. Stage 1 history: on 2026-09-02 the suites were found unrun and partly broken (a frontend test reading a file deleted in 3a4ac3a, two tests importing bun:test, one Rust test failing on an f32 round trip); issue #1 fixed them, added the `test` and `typecheck` scripts and the `packageManager` pin, and Stage 1 now runs the full suites. `cargo test --workspace` needs the llama-helper sidecar in frontend/src-tauri/binaries (see Stage 2 prerequisites); 3 Rust tests are #[ignore] on Linux by design. Stage 2 prerequisites: the llama-helper sidecar must be built and copied first (`cargo build --release -p llama-helper` then copy target/release/llama-helper to frontend/src-tauri/binaries/llama-helper-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, exactly the CI step); ffmpeg is fetched by build.rs. Release facts that matter for delivery: release.yml builds macOS and Windows only, Linux bundles exist only as CI artifacts; the updater endpoint, Homebrew cask and Scoop bucket still point at bykof/conversationaly (upstream), not at this fork - a rebrand issue, not a Stage 2 step.

verification.//stage2: The boundary is the installed desktop application: the AppImage built from the tree under test, launched natively on Wayland on a clean profile (fresh HOME/XDG dirs) as a first-time user would. Evidence comes through Orca's computer-use CLI (`orca-ide`; the `orca` shim is broken on this machine, and bare `orca` is the GNOME screen reader) reading the app's AT-SPI accessibility tree. The first pass checks the app starts: the process is alive, it is listed as an app, it has one top-level window with the configured title, the first-launch screen exposes a 'Welcome to ...' heading and a 'Get Started' push button, and the stdout log reports setup complete without a panic. The Linux computer-use provider takes no screenshots, so there is no pixel evidence. The second pass checks audio actually flows, which until #8 no verdict could: scripts/audio-harness.sh makes a PipeWire virtual source the default input and loops a speech sample into it, and scripts/stage2-record-check.sh drives a fresh profile through onboarding and a recording and asserts the sample's words come back as a transcript. The observation is the transcript, not the absence of errors: a harness feeding silence passes every liveness check and fails this one, which is why the harness refuses to report success unless it measures signal. Cost: a clean profile downloads about 4.3 GB before it can record (the transcription model gates recording; a summary model starts on the same screen and is not gated), so this pass takes roughly ten minutes plus the download. The audio pass needs a live PipeWire session and therefore does not run in CI. System audio is covered by the harness but is not run on every gate: `scripts/audio-harness.sh up --system-only --system-home <profile>/home` plus `BC_PREFERRED_SYSTEM_DEVICE='backchannel harness system monitor capture (output)' scripts/stage2-record-check.sh ...` was verified end to end on 2026-09-03 -- the application opened the device and transcribed it while the real microphone delivered silence, so the audio can only have arrived through the system channel. It is left out of the default pass because each app run costs about ten minutes plus its downloads, and a gate nobody waits for is a gate nobody runs; run it by hand when a change touches the system-audio path. What is still not covered: both channels at once, transcription quality, and macOS and Windows (ADR 0005).
verification.//stage1-ignored: cpal_capture_round_trip stays #[ignore]d because it needs a real input device and microphone permission, which GitHub runners do not have — the CI suites must keep passing without it. It runs here instead, where the machine does have one. It is the guard for the class where enumeration and lookup disagree about a device's identity (#9, #10); it was written, ignored, and therefore did not catch #9. Note it asserts a sample count, not signal: on this machine the capture path returns exact zeros, so a full count of silence passes it.
